Alm.et: The form suggests a Bavarian influence (cf. German Taube vs Bavarian Daum (“dove”)). From Middle High German alben, the oblique form of albe, from Old High German alba. Doublet of Alp. Compare Bavarian Alm, Alemannic German Alp, Alpe.

Alman.et: Borrowed from Turkish Alman (“German”), ultimately from French Allemand.

Almanach.et:
First attested in the 16th century. Borrowed from Middle Dutch almanag (Flanders 1426), from Medieval Latin almanach (1267), from Andalusian Arabic مَنَاخ (manāḵ, “calendar”).
The Ibero-Arabic term is of uncertain origin. See also almanaque. Perhaps originally…
